craft_notes: Sthāyin: the charge (five refusals). Abhinavagupta frame: karuṇa-sthāyin carried by anubhāva-catalogue (the refusals listed ARE the feeling showing); śruti-turn rendered straight — sincere-vs-ironic held open per UNC (tipping either way kills a reading; vighna rule: importing irony the Sanskrit only suggests would wall the sahṛdaya from one whole rasa). Rows: 1 (āha placed late — ‘declares’ carries the turn), 7 (uttamāṅga kept after first verb, mirroring brūṣe nottamāṅga), 9 (na-anaphora → ‘not’-anaphora; doctrine-catalogue answers with ‘without’-anaphora — complaint-music converted into doctrine-music, which IS the verse’s move), 10 (śruti left standing, no gloss). Close: ‘and the rest’ — the ādi-catalogue refusing to close IS the doctrine. Rejected: ironic tip — killed by UNC; trimming refusals — killed: five ARE the charge; closing on ‘You’ — killed: weak landing, Sanskrit lands on śrutiḥ/āha. Read aloud: YOU-speak-NOT … YOU-look-NOT … YOU-hear-NOT — yet SCRIP-ture TRU-ly de-CLARES.

lines: You speak not, O Fair-limbed. You look not on wretched me.
You hear not my oft-made plea, nor come into my mind.
Fallen into the pit mid-ocean of becoming, mostly unsupported —
yet scripture truly declares You without speech, without sight, without hearing, without feet, and the rest.

notes: śruti turn rendered straight; sincere-vs-ironic open — see argmap

reads_against.argmap: Five refusals charged — speak, see, hear, come, support — and scripture converts the charge into doctrine: the Lord is sense-free. → Complaint becomes doctrine: denial becomes declaration.
